title: Relative Leray spectral sequence for module direct images of ringed topoi
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D,\mathcal E$ be sites small in a common universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], with sheaves of commutative rings $\mathcal O_{\mathcal C},\mathcal O_{\mathcal D},\mathcal O_{\mathcal E}$. Let $a:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),\mathcal O_{\mathcal C})\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),\mathcal O_{\mathcal D})$ and $b:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),\mathcal O_{\mathcal D})\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal E),\mathcal O_{\mathcal E})$ be morphisms of ringed topoi [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Work in module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and compute higher direct images by injective resolutions [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. For every $\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}$-module $M$ there is a natural first-quadrant cohomological spectral sequence of $\mathcal O_{\mathcal E}$-modules $$E_2^{p,q}=R^pb_*(R^qa_*M)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad R^{p+q}(b\circ a)_*M.$$ For each total degree $m\geq0$, convergence supplies a finite decreasing filtration of the abutment with graded pieces $E_\infty^{p,m-p}$. No flatness of either structural ring morphism is assumed.

proof.text: Apply the ring-sheaf Grothendieck theorem to each of the three small ringed sites. Their module categories are Grothendieck abelian; hence the enough-injectives theorem gives injective resolutions in the source and intermediate categories (and also the target). These are the categories and resolutions required for the composable-pair theorem.

source.place: Tag 079Q (remark-existence-D), module categories; existence of injectives in Grothendieck categories

proof.text: Put $F=a_*$ and $G=b_*$. The underlying set direct images are right adjoints. For a limit cone, the adjunction identifies maps into its image with compatible families of maps into its entries, so these direct images preserve finite limits. Module kernels and finite products are created on the underlying sheaves (kernels are sectionwise); consequently the induced module direct images preserve kernels and finite products, hence are left exact. They are additive: the image of a sum of module maps is the sum of the images, since addition is the map out of the product induced by sheaf addition. Finally $(b\circ a)_*=b_*a_*$ on underlying sheaves. Its scalar action is the composite $\mathcal O_{\mathcal E}\to b_*\mathcal O_{\mathcal D}\to b_*a_*\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}$, exactly the action of the composite ringed morphism, so this is also the canonical identification on module sheaves.

For every injective source module $I$, the total-acyclicity theorem for $a$ gives $H^q(K,a_*I)=0$ for every sheaf of sets $K$ on $\mathcal D$ and $q>0$. Apply the totally-acyclic direct-image theorem with $f=b$ and $N=a_*I$. It gives $R^pb_*(a_*I)=0$ for $p>0$. Thus $F$ sends injectives to $G$-acyclics, precisely the acyclicity hypothesis of the composable pair. Neither input assumes flatness; no preservation of injectives by $a_*$ has been asserted.

The Grothendieck spectral-sequence theorem now applies to $(F,G)$ and $M$, yielding naturally in $M$ the first-quadrant page $E_2^{p,q}=R^pb_*(R^qa_*M)$ and abutment $R^{p+q}(b_*a_*)M$. Step 2 identifies this with $R^{p+q}(b\circ a)_*M$: applying the identified functors to the same source injective resolution gives identified complexes and cohomology. For the filtration, use the double-complex realization included in that theorem and its convergence theorem: its filtration has $\mathrm{Fil}^0H^m=H^m$, $\mathrm{Fil}^{m+1}H^m=0$, and $\mathrm{Fil}^pH^m/\mathrm{Fil}^{p+1}H^m\cong E_\infty^{p,m-p}$. All objects and subquotients lie in the target module category, so this is the required finite module filtration.
